override.reason: Both functions' line counts are dominated by multi-line actionable failure prose the standard mandates be present at the failure point, not by branching. Logic depth in each is one linear pass with no nesting beyond a single loop; extracting the message strings would move mandated text away from the site the standard puts it at.

smells.finding: No classes beyond two NamedTuples (Violation, ApprovedEntry), each 4 and 3 fields.

RETIRED_PATHS (scripts/verify_retirement.py:96) and RETIRED_NAMES (:107) independently encode the same retirement facts: 3 of the 5 retired paths have their basename restated in RETIRED_NAMES (apply_lessons_delta, verify_lessons_applied, verify_agent_feedback), and LESSONS.md / AGENT_FEEDBACK.md are the basenames of the other two. A future retirement that adds a path but forgets the name silently loses the content leg for it, and nothing in the test suite catches the omission -- test_every_leg_has_a_red_proof pins the leg roster, not the contents of these two tuples. Advisory: derive the overlapping names from RETIRED_PATHS, or add a census test asserting every RETIRED_PATHS basename appears in RETIRED_NAMES.
The _leg_* functions operate on the module's own constants and its own _read_lines/normalize helpers; no reaching into another module's data.

store_mention_sites (scripts/verify_retirement.py:323) returns list[tuple[str, int, str]] -- a bare (path, line, mention) triple -- while the same module models both of its other triples/quads as NamedTuples (Violation, ApprovedEntry) precisely so callers read fields by name. _leg_store_mention then unpacks it positionally. Minor and local, but it is the one place the module departs from its own stated convention. Advisory only.

Exclusions are dict[str, str] where the KEY's string shape silently selects the matching algorithm: is_shipped (:168) treats a key ending in '/' as a path prefix and any other key as an fnmatch glob restricted to root level. That convention exists only inside is_shipped -- a reader of SCOPE_EXCLUSIONS (:144) cannot tell from the constant that 'notes-*.md' is root-only, nor how many files it reaches. This is not hypothetical: it is the direct cause of BLOCKING/ADVISORY finding 2, where the entry's own reason names three files while the glob removes seven tracked files plus every future one. A small Exclusion type (or separate PREFIX_/GLOB_ constants) would make the reach visible at the declaration.
Maximum arity across all 17 functions in the guard is 2.
Three new files, no existing file touched; there is no change scattered across callers.
The module has one axis of change -- what counts as retired -- and its constants are grouped by that axis.
No chained navigation; the deepest access is spine.get('tasks', {}) guarded by an isinstance check.
main() exposes a --root argument no shipped caller passes.

override.repo_standard: references/global-everyone.md, Deep-module vocabulary: 'The interface is the test surface. Test through it, not past it.'
override.reason: --root is what makes scan() testable through its public interface against decoy repositories rather than by monkeypatching module state; the per-leg red-proofs all depend on a caller-supplied root. It is a required test seam with a real second implementer (every decoy), not an unused generalization.

smells.finding: 76 comment-only lines plus heavy docstrings across 580 lines -- roughly a third of the module is prose.

override.repo_standard: epic-418 scope-discipline ruling as restated in the g1 handoff: 'A corner case you choose not to chase gets a comment at the code site naming it, and is reported up -- never silently absorbed'; plus the module's own required-reason rule (_require_reasons) making every exclusion carry a written justification.
override.reason: Fowler's smell is comments compensating for code that fails to explain itself. These comments carry design HISTORY that the code cannot express -- which legs a cold panel already measured green and cut, why 'tracked' beats 'exists', why ast beats import and regex, and the two CORNER CASE, NOT CHASED notices the repo standard positively requires at the code site. Removing them would violate a documented standard, and the code would still read the same.
